hero.title: Keep your debts clear and your agreements balanced.

product.title: Two ways to keep track of a debt. You choose.
product.lead: Start by writing your debts down just for yourself. When both sides are ready, turn them into an agreement that you both confirm.

personal.title: Personal record
personal.text: Write down what you owe and what you are owed. Nobody else takes part or needs an account: the balance is the one you record.
personal.p2: Edit and correct it whenever you like.
personal.p3: Always labelled as a personal record.

shared.title: Shared agreement
shared.text: You propose the terms and share a link. The other person accepts them, rejects them or asks for changes. Only what you both confirm counts.
shared.p1: Both sides accept the very same version.
shared.p2: Every payment is confirmed by the other side.
shared.p3: What is confirmed can no longer be altered.

product.bridge: And you can move from one to the other: invite someone to confirm a personal record whenever you like, without losing what you already had.

legend.title: One symbol that tells you how much weight a figure carries
legend.lead: Each half is one of the two sides. A filled half means that side stands behind it.

personal.title: Your records, for your eyes only
personal.lead: Record what you owe and what you are owed without asking anything of anybody. The other person does not even need an account.

p1.title: What you owe and what you are owed
p1.text: Organised by person, with concept, amount, start date and due date.

p2.title: Payments and partial payments
p2.text: Every payment updates the balance you keep on record.

p3.title: Notes, receipts and reminders
p3.text: Due-date reminders reach you and nobody else.

p4.title: Correct it whenever you like
p4.text: They are your records: edit or delete them without anybody’s approval, and every change stays in your history.

personal.note: A personal record is never presented as something the other side has confirmed.

card.reminder: Reminder for you: due on Friday
card.private: Marta needs no account and is not notified

shared.title: When you both want it in writing
shared.lead: Turn a debt into an agreement that both sides confirm. It all starts with a link.
shared.stepsLabel: How a shared agreement comes together

s1.title: Propose the terms
s1.text: Amount, dates and how it will be paid. You can start from a personal record: the original stays untouched.

s2.title: Share the link
s2.text: Send it by WhatsApp, email or any way you like. The other person opens it and signs in with Google.

s3.title: You both answer
s3.text: They can accept, reject or ask for changes. The agreement only takes effect when both of you accept the very same version.

shared.n1: Every important change creates a new version that both must accept.
shared.n2: If somebody you did not expect opens the link, you decide: confirm they are the right person, or turn them away before the agreement becomes active.
shared.n3: When you convert a personal record, your earlier payments are not taken as confirmed: the other person explicitly accepts the ones you want recognised.
shared.n4: Disagreements have their place: you can flag a dispute, or cancel by mutual agreement.

payments.title: Every payment, with how and when
payments.lead: Cash, transfer, deposit or card: write it down the way it happened. Symmetry Debt does not move money; it only keeps count.

p1.title: Two dates, no confusion
p1.text: It keeps when it was paid and when it was recorded.

p2.title: As much detail as you need
p2.text: Reference and tracking key for transfers; where it was handed over for cash.

p3.title: Mistakes are corrected, not erased
p3.text: A payment that is already confirmed is corrected with an adjustment or a reversal that both approve.

p4.title: Your bank accounts stay private
p4.text: Save your CLABE (it is validated as you type) and share the details to receive a payment only when you authorise it.

track.title: The path of a payment in a shared agreement

s1.title: One side records it
s1.text: Whoever pays or whoever receives, it makes no difference.

s2.title: It waits to be validated
s2.text: The confirmed balance does not change yet.

s3.title: The other side answers
s3.text: They confirm, reject or ask for a clarification.

track.result: Once confirmed, it counts towards the confirmed balance.
track.alt: If it is rejected, it stays in the history and does not count.

installments.title: Instalments, without losing count
installments.lead: A single date, weekly or monthly payments, or instalments of your own. For each one you see how much is scheduled, paid and pending.
installments.p1: Early and partial payments are applied to the instalments in order.
installments.p2: Overdue instalments stay in plain sight.
installments.p3: You can reschedule: in a shared agreement, both accept the new calendar.
installments.p4: Progress is worked out from your records or, in a shared agreement, from confirmed payments only.

card.label: Illustration with fictional data: a plan of four monthly instalments, one paid, one overdue with a partial payment and two upcoming.
card.title: Payment plan

receipts.title: Receipts within reach
receipts.lead: Attach a PDF or a photo to a debt, a payment or an adjustment. They are always optional.

p1.title: PDF, JPG, PNG and WebP
p1.text: The file is checked to be what it claims to be, with a size limit.

p2.title: Private storage
p2.text: Only those who can see the debt can open them. With preview and download.

p3.title: Evidence, not confirmation
p3.text: A receipt does not confirm a payment by itself: in a shared agreement, the other side still has to confirm it.

card.label: Illustration with fictional data: a payment waiting to be validated, with a PDF receipt attached.
card.note: The receipt goes with the payment. The validation comes from the other side.

security.title: Private by design
security.lead: What you write down for yourself stays with you. What you share is up to you.

i1.title: Your personal records are yours alone
i1.text: Nobody else can see them, not even the person they mention.

i2.title: An email address opens no doors
i2.text: Somebody knowing your email or your name does not let them see or claim your records.

i3.title: Agreements between two, and only two
i3.text: A shared agreement is visible only to the two people who are part of it.

i4.title: Encrypted bank details
i4.text: Your CLABE and account number are stored encrypted. We never ask for passwords, PINs or CVVs.

i5.title: What is confirmed is not rewritten
i5.text: What both confirmed is never edited or deleted: it is corrected with a new movement, in plain sight of both.

i6.title: Your data, whenever you want it
i6.text: Download all your data or delete your account from Settings.

i7.title: Google sign-in, no passwords
i7.text: We store no passwords or Google account credentials, and you can sign out on all your devices.

i8.title: No ads, no trackers
i8.text: The app includes no advertising and no third-party tracking services.

openSource.title: Open, so you can trust it
openSource.lead: Symmetry Debt is free software under the MIT licence. Anyone can read the code, suggest improvements or install it on their own server.

p1.title: Genuinely free
p1.text: No paid plans, no locked features.

p2.title: Host it yourself
p2.text: It includes what you need to run it with Docker on your own domain and database.

p3.title: No lock-in
p3.text: Your data exports in an open format you can read without the app.

p4.title: In Spanish and in English
p4.text: The app, the documentation and the emails.

share.title: Symmetry Debt
share.text: Clear debts and agreements between two people. Free, private and open source.

q1.q: Do I have to invite the other person to use it?
q1.a: No. You can keep your debts as personal records, just for yourself. The other person needs no account and is not notified.

q2.q: What is the difference between a personal record and a shared agreement?
q2.a: A personal record is what you write down: it helps you stay organised, but nobody else has confirmed it. In a shared agreement both sides accept the same terms and every payment is confirmed by the other side. The app never presents one as if it were the other.

q3.q: How does the other person find out about an agreement?
q3.a: Creating the agreement generates a link that you send them any way you like. They open it, sign in with Google, review the terms and decide whether to accept them, reject them or ask for changes.

q4.q: Can I turn a personal record into a shared agreement?
q4.a: Yes. You choose what to share and a proposal is created. Your earlier payments are not taken as confirmed: the other person has to explicitly accept the ones you want recognised. If they do not accept, your personal record stays exactly as it was.

q5.q: Does Symmetry Debt move money or connect to my bank?
q5.a: No. It only keeps the record of debts and payments. You pay the way you always do (cash, transfer or deposit) and write it down here.

q6.q: What if we disagree about a payment?
q6.a: The other side can reject it or ask for a clarification. A rejected payment does not count towards the confirmed balance, and everything stays in the history. If the disagreement is bigger, the agreement can be flagged as disputed.

q7.a: Your personal records: only you. A shared agreement: only the two people who are part of it. Your bank accounts are private, and the other side sees the details to pay you only if you authorise it.

q8.a: Nothing. It is free and open source, under the MIT licence. There are no paid plans and no locked features.

q9.q: Can I install it on my own server?
q9.a: Yes. The code includes what you need to install it with Docker on your own domain, with your own database.

q10.q: Can I export or delete my data?
q10.a: Yes. From Settings you can download all your data and delete your account.
